problem: VLM-based VLN agents struggle with consistent temporal grounding and robust perception-action mapping; step-wise or rule-based fixed reasoning is costly and causes overthinking, while learning adaptive reasoning via SFT needs large costly embodied data.
motivation: Ideal agents should decide when and how to reason, but VLMs are overconfident and cannot perceive task difficulty, and embodied reasoning traces are expensive. The authors observe that action entropy along a trajectory correlates with failure, giving a cheap interpretable difficulty signal.
key_idea: Use historical action entropy as an uncertainty prior to drive a lightweight reasoning-mode selector (UAR block), trained with a Heuristic-to-RL schedule that anneals the entropy prior into a learned RL policy.
insight: Sustained high entropy (not instantaneous spikes) separates failed from successful trajectories, so it is a good cold-start prior for triggering reasoning. Ablation (NaVid base, R2R-CE): fixed-interval reasoning SR 40.12 and random 39.5, no RL 42.53, no heuristic prior 43.82, full 47.7, so both adaptive gating and prior+RL matter. With more training the agent reasons less (about 2.5 times per 55-step trajectory) and 71% of reasoning triggers fall on hard episodes.
method: Action Entropy: mean token-level entropy of the generated action tokens; history H_{<=t} combined with the current entropy state serves as the uncertainty signal

UAR Block: lightweight linear plugin p_mode = W1*H_{<=t} + W2*o_t + W3*I + b, softmax over {no reasoning, description, summary, error correction}; the reasoning text is generated by the same VLM as the navigation policy
Uncertainty-based prior: soft distribution over modes from |mean past entropy - tau_k|/sigma with thresholds tau_k = tau_0 + k*delta (tau_0 is a percentile of entropy on 1,000 val episodes)
Heuristic-to-RL transition: p_final = lambda_t*p_prior + (1-lambda_t)*p_mode, with lambda annealed 1 to 0 over training

Reward: geodesic distance-reduction reward minus a normalized reasoning-length cost (relative to the shortest successful generation in the group), discounted return; group rollouts (5 per episode), lr 1e-6
Plugged into NaVid and NaVILA; trained on only 3K R2R + 3K RxR episodes (6K in total)

setting.backbone: NaVid (Vicuna-based) and NaVILA (VLM), fine-tuned with the UAR block via RL
setting.training_data: 6K episodes (3K R2R + 3K RxR train) added on top of the base models' own data (NaVid 550K, NaVILA ~3M); cross-dataset run uses 3K R2R only
setting.observation: monocular RGB video only (no depth, odometry or panorama)
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: turn left/right (angle), move forward (distance), stop
setting.privileged: none at test time (geodesic distance is used only in the training reward)

numbers.extra: +6K training episodes on top of NaVILA (~3000K)
+6K training episodes on top of NaVid (550K)
AdaNav trained on 3K R2R only, evaluated on RxR-CE without RxR training

numbers_note: Real-world results (Table 5, NaVILA-AdaNav SR 82.5/73.5 meeting room sample/complex, 95/88 home, 87.6/75.5 office) and ScanQA results are also reported but do not fit the canonical benchmarks. Table 1 uses the R2R-CE/RxR-CE benchmark in the paper's own naming.
results: With only 6K extra episodes, NaVILA-AdaNav reaches 60.19 SR / 50.0 SPL on R2R-CE val-unseen, beating the strongest closed-source baseline MonoDream (55.8 SR / 49.1 SPL) and base NaVILA (54.0 SR). On RxR-CE it gets 49.8 SR (vs NaVILA 44.0, MonoDream 49.4), and about 11.4% real-world SR gains over the base models.
limitations: Evaluated only on two base models (NaVid, NaVILA) with a small, hand-defined set of three reasoning modes
Difficulty analysis defines hard episodes as those the base model fails, and reasoning text quality is not evaluated independently; real-world trials are few (25 instructions per scene, 3 runs)
Hyperparameter tables show the reported default configuration is not the best (SR up to about 49.6), suggesting limited tuning or noise
